speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) over the last three years, what average percentage of GST paid by the lowest 20% of households (by income) is offset by all forms of GST vouchers; and (b) what is the breakdown based on one-off versus permanent GST voucher schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The GST Voucher (GSTV) is one permanent scheme that provides support to lower and middle income households and seniors for their living expenses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: It comprises an annual cash payout, annual MediSave top-up for those aged 65 and above and quarterly utilities rebates (U-Save) for Housing and Development Board (HDB) households.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In some years, there were additional one-off GSTV special payments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: This was the case in the past three years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In 2019, a GSTV – Cash special payment was given to celebrate Singapore's bicentennial and to support Singaporeans who need more help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: An additional $20 of U-Save rebate was also provided each year from 2019 to 2021 to mitigate the impact of the introduction of the carbon tax.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In 2020, additional U-Save rebates were given to all eligible HDB households to help Singaporeans cope during the extraordinary uncertainty brought about suddenly by COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: An enhanced GSTV scheme will continue to be part of the progressive system of taxes and transfers that we have in Singapore, ensuring that lower income households receive more benefits than the taxes that they pay.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Especially in light of COVID-19, I think there is a lot of concern as to inequality, especially if you look at the household income from work, I think it is the lowest 10% that saw the hardest hit in terms of income.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, in terms of the supplementary questions, I have got two.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is in relation to the enhanced permanent GST Voucher scheme, in terms of the target amount of offset for the households involved, what is the target in terms of how much of the GST that would have been payable and how much of it do you want to offset?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: And what is the percentage of Singaporeans that will come under this GST Voucher scheme?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The second is also in relation to that.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: If I look at the cut-off right now, in terms of the assessible income criterion, that is about $28,000, which works out to about $2,300 a month, which is significantly lower than the median monthly income from work of about $4,500.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, I just want to understand, in terms of the scope of this permanent GST Voucher scheme, the amount of help that could be rendered to the middle income households.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Inequality is certainly an issue that the Government is very focused on.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been tackling this issue through a whole range of measures – Workfare, GST Vouchers, Senior Employment Credit, a whole range of different social support measures – for at least 20 years now.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And you can see from the statistics that, in fact, the Gini coefficient in Singapore, post-tax and transfers, has been coming down.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to do more to address inequality and social mobility, particularly, given that the concerns of COVID-19 and the impact of the pandemic are being felt disproportionately more by the lower income groups.
